reviews.text: Great natural park in the middle of the city. Its fun to visit in the evening and see people going through data of other kids to get their kids married. Park is filled with street food and street market on one side, tea house on the other where people are playing cards, ganes or just enjoying the lake view with their tea.

It's such an interesting place to experience local culture. Tea houses everywhere, locals playing cards and of course... the famous "parents' matchmaking corner"! Quite an eye-opener. Such a lively, authentic slice of Chengdu life. Really enjoyed just wandering and watching.

Great place to hang out and relax during the weekend or weekday, whenever you have free time. There is a lot going on, when I went they had a chrysanthemum festival/competition. Theres plenty of stalls for quick snacks, and many tea houses for afternoon tea. Highly recommend coming here to relax, go have a tea and sunflower seeds at a teahouse and enjoy a face changing show, it embodies the relaxed Chengdu lifestyle.

This is a refreshing urban green space and a key hub for local social life. The park features peaceful Chinese-style pavilion, a large sparkling pond, gentle hills, colorful gardens, and sculptures. The Local Scene: Locals gather here daily to socialize and relax, enjoying tea, or even participating in group exercises, including line dancing and choreographed performances, contributing to the park's lively, bustling atmosphere. Major Highlight: Heming Teahouse The Heming Teahouse is essential for experiencing local, slow-paced tea culture. For an extra cost, visitors can watch the tea-pouring shows, where tea masters skillfully pour tea using long-spouted teapots from impressive angles. It's an one of its kind cultural demonstration. Spoiler alert: Hidden Gem: The Chengdu No.1 Air-Raid Shelter This is a hidden gem that often overlooked by most. This historical war museum originally built for civil defense, the shelter maintains a consistent 25°C year-round, making it a quiet and cool place to learn about wartime history. Accessibility: The park is easily accessible via People's Park Station on Line 2. Turn RIGHT at Exit B; the North Entrance is just a short walk away.

Get away from the hustle bustle of the city scape here. You will see how the folks here doing morning exercises, having tea while enjoying the surroundings. Beautiful place to be. There's also a matchmaking corner.

Beautiful and living parc, you can see dances, playing people or just some parents looking after someone for their child, by marital ads. I'd recommend to test a tea house there, we were quite lucky to see different dancers in a show.

Great place to walk and people watch. The park itself is beautiful, bustling with activities of all sorts; various performances, old people dancing, boating at the lake, etc.. The tea house was packed and unfortunately, we couldn't find a table so we just explored other areas. It was interesting to see the area where they post personal details on boards of men and women looking for a partner. Our guide translated some of them and the details include things like annual salaries, their properties, cars and some even have pictures on them. To be fair, according to our guide, most of the details are posted by the parents without the knowledge of their children 😀

We spent 10 days in Chengdu as part of a international delegation showcasing basketry at the Intangible Cultural Heritage Festival. As such we had not much time to explore the city at all but on our last morning, before our transfers back to the airport we wanted to go out and spend some time in a "green" area. The Peoples park looked interesting and close to a subway station so we choose this one. It was a very hot day and as soon as we entered one of the lovely paved walkways the temperature dropped a few degrees. As "western" people we loved the way the whole park is centered around the big lake but also offers shaded bamboo groves, and even a wonderful Bonsai Garden. There were plenty of stalls to buy a refreshment and even tea gardens. There is also a kind of "marriage" grove were people can pin their classified ads on fences with their details and hope for love. Rather fascinating. We spent about 2 hours there and loved every minute.

Visiting this place helped me change my views on China! This place was awesome, such a great area to meet with friends, hang out by yourself, enjoy some tea, get your ears cleaned! The "Marriage market" was interesting, my tour guide translated some of the postings to us. The park is massive and has lots of different areas to check out, there was dancing going on, and market stalls. Definitely check this place out!

A huge, clean, and safe park that has lovely flower beds, monuments, teashops, souvenir stalls, etc. There's a section for Singles who are looking for potential spouses, a kind of Tinder on paper. The pink papers are females looking for suitable males whereas the blue papers are males looking for females. All in Chinese of course but a google translation can be quite amusing.
Excellent place for a morning walk. Tea houses and lots of space. Be sure to visit if you are in Cheng Du.

This is a pleasant park to walk through - has nice view with the small lake, restaurants to eat at, lots of activities by the locals. Really get to see the culture of the city in one. Has a bit of everything!
Beautiful park, with some attractions like amusement park for kids, the boat rent in the lake, some artists doing presentations and food stalls options.

The People's Park is very crowded but interesting place small groups of people dancing other groups of people exercising there were places to sit and have tea the tea was very expensive there were other places that had street food to street food was inexpensive we enjoyed our visit it was easy to be dropped off by a taxi or pick up a taxi at the entrance to the park
We came in the evening and it was raining. The lanterns looked very pretty. There were a few street sellers selling tea and other snacks.

Very large parks with 2 tea house. Would recommend getting a long spout tea dance at one of the tea house. Tasty tea and a fun little show. The park was very busy when we visited, so maybe not as relaxing as it could be. But worth a visit

I really enjoyed spending a couple of hours in peoples park. A pretty lake, nice paths to walk around with some landmarks and a bonsai garden. Lovely to spend a couple hours in the Heming Tea House and have some tea by the water.
Very beautiful park in the city where people come to chill, meet, and engage in more activities; it's a must-visit place..
This is a nice park, you can eat and drink tea too.. Also they have marriage market here...

Good sized park that draws quite a big crowd, though we only visited for awhile since we were put off by the massive crowd at the only dining/tea area. We did get ourselves some souvenirs from the souvenir shop though, which had some “scroll-like” magnets which was a first. Definitely a good walk from Kuan Zai Alley or even Tianfu Square after your meals 😊

Nice park in the middle of the city. It was pretty quiet aside from the hustle and bustle of everyone walking around enjoying the park. There is a lot of green here and many older style structures to walk through and around. There are also amusement rides here. However, we didn't stop to try them out. Instead, we walked through a little bonsai tree area, watched some people kick around a hacky sack with feathers, and watched a movie/television crew film something in front of the older buildings.
Interesting place , so local feel, if you are not rush for other places, can spend a relax afternoon here.
City of Panda Chengdu, Delicious and also affordable foods, Kind people, Various things to enjoy!

One of the highlights of Chengdu. What a lovely park! Something for everyone here. Teahouse, row boats, flower and bonsai gardens, children's play areas, green spaces, matchmaking / romance park. A memorable experience.

Great way to wile away a relaxing morning or afternoon. Loved strolling around the gardens, seeing all the trees leaves' autumn colours, watching the water calligraphers, martial arts practitoners, and the general chilled vibes. This is the real local Chengdu in action. The park also contains a cool tea house, restaurant, a small street market, and a small fun-fair. The matchmakers corner (an open-air dating app) is a must-visit too.
You can have a nice walk there during night or day. You can take a rest there or have a tea in garden. You can also find a wife or husband. There is a lot of insertion:). Enjoy you visit.

The People's Park tends to get crowded on weekends. It boasts numerous tea shops where you can savor your tea, and they provide a complimentary hot water flask for refills. Additionally, you'll find food stalls, souvenir shops, and public toilets on-site. Autumn is the ideal season to visit the park.

We arrived at the People’s Park at Chengdu (成都人民公园) and stayed here for an hour. This was also “part of the trip that we didn’t pay” for as we didn’t sign up for the river cruise this evening. Read our post 2 days back where we expressed our displeasure about what was mentioned to the tour group. Nonetheless, we arrived at People’s Park where we spent an hour checking out the sights and sounds. It was a Tuesday afternoon, yet it was SO crowded! We were told about the match-making corner at People’s Park Chengdu and that was where we headed to first. There, we found that there were 2 sections. The “pink” area would be where the ladies data were, for the relatives of the men to look at. The data usually includes age, height, description of the individual and what they are looking for as a partner. Likewise, the “blue” area would be where you’d see the men’s data. It was also interesting to see that ages were across a spectrum. Younger ones for their first marriage, middle age ones for remarrying or late marriage as well as the older ones (in 50s/60s) – looking for a partner... For the full review, visit 2bearbear today!
One of the famous parks in Chengdu, has an amusement park, tea houses and a spot for public matchmaking.
An oasis in the city with soany people enjoying outdoor activities in uniquely Chinese ways. Great lake, tea shops, gardens, amazing!

Beautiful park in the middle of the city … there were a lot of performances the day we were there: dancing, music, plays. Plenty of amenities including food and toilets. The green spaces and water really make this an enjoyable place to relax.

This isn't just a park it's THE park. Park, cafe, rowing pond, food and katra market, playground, sports ground, museum, art gallery, dating centre and the list goes on. There's a section in this park full of marriage cvs from men and women of varying ages and backgrounds. The people of Chengdu come to advertise themselves and browse for a spouse. Dating apps who? These people live in the real world 😘 If my visa permitted I could probs live in this park.

A bustling park with lots of activities going on! You can paddle a kayak down a lake, enjoy the teahouse while picking ear or simply walk around the park. There is a really unique feature of this park which is the matchmaking event which goes on all year round (see video). Profiles of male/female are hung up to seek for future spouse.

I like this park. It is big with lots of people though. There is a big pond where you can rent a boat and row in it. There is also a big open tea area where you can eat in the open and have tea and enjoy the park. Only problem is that there are too, too many people. What I find really interesting are the rows and rows of board with all the A4 sized paper of singles looking for partners on these boards. Quite entertaining if you can read Chinese.

A peaceful park in centre of Chengdu City. You can enjoy the local folks dance, and the peaceful vibe here. The iconic thing is to try the Chinese afternoon tea with the large cup brewing method. Fabulous atmosphere with beautiful scenery.

A leisure and morning exercises garden for the locals, traditional cup tea for friends to catch-up over local timsum and bits. A premium tea price for tea demonstration. Ear cleansing if keen. Mahjong places for some interested. Large pond of tranquility, enjoy singing birds and feeding of carps.
Founded in 1911, it is the first public place in China to be called a park. If you want to experience the slow life of old Chengdu, People's Park is a must-visit place.
A nice park in the middle of the city, and it has a lot of outdoor restaurants near the lake for tea. A nice place to go for tourist who want to chill. It also house some museum and memorial statue.

Pleasant park. We were on a group tour and our guide brought us to look at the personal ads put up there which was interesting. There is also a lovely tea house where you can experience the Chengdu lifestyle of enjoying tea.
Good place to hangout...got lake for paddle boat...kids playground...multiple yoga taichi place...hall..food booth...

Have never seen a park so busy! What a nice experience. Just a short walk from Chengdu Musuem. You see many people dancing and also the section where you will get to see all the eligible ladies and gentlemen profile in pink and the potential parents hoping to find one suitable for their children. Highly interesting to know such thing still exist! A must visit.

This is a green belt in the city that offers locals and visitors a place to slow down the pace of life and destress. There are many trees and beautiful flowers around this big park, with the nice and cute dragon displays (it's the year of the dragon) with artful landscaping, bonsai garden, tea houses, kiddie amusement rides, a pond with row and motor boats. It is tranquil. And there are monuments to commemorate those who perished during the Xinhai Revoluntionaries and Anti-Japanese era. You will find that time has stopped temporarily here and you can enjoy in the quietness over a cup of tea, while enjoying the tea pouring demonstration or the pond to relax and recharge!

Visiting my family in Chengdu in October right before Covid. This park is the best place to hang out with friends and friendly locals. Full experience of bliss, peace, harmony, and content at ease in cultural essence of Sichuan style. Beautiful landscapes, well designed gardens, variety of flowers and plants, architectures of Ming/Qing styles and the most importantly happy crowds of people; seniors, kids, teens, young folks, all walks of life; Singing, dancing, playing, wandering, laughing, napping, chatting, eating and so much more. You can always find something you enjoy here. I have been there so many times at different seasons and will always go back whenever I’m in town.

In the city center. Metro and bus are available. Good place for tea, you can also enjoy the Chinese Kongfu Tea Show and the Sichuan Opera Face show. Local people like to stay in the tea house for a day. Casual life with good view and good tea.

- free entry - easy to access with multiple entrances and exits - toilets and water filling stations available - beautiful place, lots of history and a vibrant feel - has multiple beautiful teahouses which sell delicious both hot and cold tea - has a small children’s fairground at the back which was fun - lots of vendors selling sweet treats and souvenirs - contains the famous marriage posters

One of the most famous park in Chengdu that the locals (and a lot of tourists) to chill, drink tea, and eat snacks. It is quite easy to get to as it is right besides People's Park station. It is a place to chill out for a couple of hours if you want to relax and enjoy the "old" chengdu lifestyle. However, I recommend skipping it if drinking tea, eating snacks, and chilling with hundreds of people is not your thing 😅 (I was there for 30 mins...)
Clean and nice place to stay for couple of hours, several new and interesting things were there for me as for a foreigner

The Chengdu city's People's Park has a most unique feature: the Matchmaking Corner where the pathways are lined with hundreds of meticulously written bios of hopeful singletons. The male profiles are on light blue paper while the females' go pink. No digital app, this is the pragmatic side of Chinese matchmaking. The quirky thing is that it's the older generations - the parents or grandparents - who browse, ask questions and negotiate! This is an unconventional, community effort to forge connections in a fast-paced world.

There’s so much going on in this park: people dancing, singing, playing cards, playing other board games, drinking tea, looking for a partner, strolling around… It is the most “eclectic” park I’ve ever been to Loved itttt!!
Nice park to experience what the local do. Lots of eateries and some performance.

This place is very good national park for walking and breath some air with a tea house and great environment. A lot of place you can go with a tons of shade and tree. This is the place you should come if the weather is great.

There were numerous groups of people performing or exercising which the audience may participate in and enjoy. Additionally, there were many tea places where you can drink and relax. I wouldn't recommend if it were just for a picnic.
A place to enjoy Chengdu's local Chinese Tea and Opera Chinese Show for a fee depending on the type of tea that you order.
You can feel Chill and nature in the morning, don't miss the match making corner in the park, it's an eye opener
We experienced local tea house athmophere and bought cute souvenirs. We walked through the park on our way to Kuan Zhai aeough Accessible by subway with its on stop.
Great place to step out from the rush of the main city! A lot of locals playing cards, dancing and chilling. My favourite park in chengdu, come and enjoy the snacks or bring your own food 😅
Wonderfully Park. Matchmakers corner, boating lake and a variety of good eating places also a tea house.
Beautiful peaceful park, although crowded in some areas. A number of tea houses and activities scattered within, so absolutely a place to visit while in Chengdu.
Nice place to unwind and sip morning tea. Can get very crowded in the afternoon.

Stroll with the locals and have some tea. Be sure to look at *both* sides of the tea menu, including the cheaper side that may not be initially shown to you. The men walking around clanging two metal rods will clean your ears for a fee. Don't miss the match-making posts section. Near the central circle find various music groups performing, with a decibel meter on a pole in the background for each one to make sure they don't get too loud.
Lovely (and lively) park in Chengdu, not too far from Tianfu Square. Various stalls for food and drink.
Great local park with places to eat and drink tea also small children's amusement park inside

A large park in the middle of Chengdu, it's very beautiful and well maintained. You can relax and drink tea, enjoy the scenery and sometimes you can see a show here. We were lucky to see a public Sichuan face changing opera here.
Expansive and serene sanctuary amidst the city’s chaos, with plenty of sheltered areas to sit and relax.
Beautiful park in the city center. A lot of people come to do lot of things. Very interesting area for an european person to discover chinese culture
Nice park in the middle of Chengdu. Good way to relax in a quiet and beautiful place
I visited People's Park at the start of this year, the environment was nice. It had a calm and peaceful atmosphere. Be sure to visit the tea house!
A busy park with few tea houses by the water. Very crowded and noisy. Interesting experience having tea and watching people.
Great experience. Boating, Tea, and more. It reminds one of Central Park in New York City.

The park is clean and well maintained, The atmosphere is energetic and at the same time feels relaxing. Locals from all walks of life - kids, students, young adults and seniors- can be seen doing their own thing here.
Great park with plenty of activities for children. Small carnival rides and boat hire. Lots of beautiful scenic gardens.
No entry fees. There is a teahouse which looks nice but extremely overcrowded. Good atmosphere overall.
Beautiful, shady area to take a break and see the local life. Also had an artificial lake and koi point, as well as a tea House
It's a nice park in the heart of everything. Reminds me of the convenience of Central Park in New York City
Great place! Very nice atmosphere and lots to see and experience! Don't miss this place when in Chengdu!

a very big park in the city centre, beautiful landscape with lots of trees, a big lake. The hundred-year tea house is right by the lake. Like many Renmin Parks in major cities, there is a place for parents to post the information of their kids for dating-matching. The monument in memorial of the "Railway Protecting Movement" happened in the late Qing Dynasty which led to the later Wuchang Uprising.

Loved the local scene here. We watched the opera, fire spitting & face changing performance. Only 58Y entrance fees & given a cup of flowered tea & huge pot of hot water. Lots of other food, snacks for sale. Best way to unwind after all the touristy stuff.
Beautiful park in the middle of a bustling city Try the tea at one of the tea houses.
Drink a famous traditional chinese tea in Peole's Park, Chengdu and do as a chinese do.

Nice park with Chinese gardens and culture activities. But was too crowded. There was a kids park. All facilities were like 40 years ago and badly maintained (well they seem just abandoned those could not be repaired). Price is high considering the “four-decade old” facility.
Beautiful park full of families on a Sunday wirh loads to do and see. Why not have your earwax removed by on one of the local vendors while you drink tea

Love the park. I grew up in Chengdu, I used to go there with my family every weekend to have tea when I was a kid. Unfortunately, I had to move to Australia more than a decade ago. I miss Chengdu and the tea culture so much!
Nice park , full of people enjoying the open green area , well equipped for activities , and plenty of retired people doing many activities

People's park is an ok park for an hour walk. It could be very crowded and noisy on the weekends. I didnt notice many places for rest and relax. The lake water didnt smell very nice so i wouldn't recommend planning too much time to visit. Seems like there were a few places to eat and have tea. Children could enjoy the amusement park.

Nice area, relaxed and quiet with market stalls in some areas, restaurants in some areas, tea rooms and across the day there is entertainment in some areas. It has also small railway protection area, bonsai garden and areas with water.

This park was great for a stroll. Unfortunately our trip got cut short due to rain. They had some old bomb (?) shelters in the park that people appeared to be visiting. There were also a lot of tea houses, and a place to rent boats.
A beautiful walk, but would recommending skipping the tea.. seems a bit overpriced although the tea places themselves are very much worth a peak.
Pretty green oasis in the heart of the city. Sunday afternoon bustling with locals sipping tea, paddling boats and perusing the craft market.

A really Nice spot in the city. Just loved the bonsai garden.lovely to see People exercising and dancing. Weird though to see somesort of parent tinder corner where parents try to match their children. Unique.... Nice pond with lots of koi fishes
The garden itself is big and wide and nice. But it's very crowded, so you can forget about relaxing quietly.
A very vibrant park with flowers, nice architectures, restaurant with performance. Very crowded too.

What an amazing park! First of all, it's free to enter ;) Secondly, so many different areas with various types of trees, flowers, plants, etc. Lastly, it wasn't that crowded and was one of the few non-touristy places I've stumbled upon.
Although its in the heart of the city, the atmosphere is relaxed. Great place to see locals just hanging out and enjoying the beauty of the park. Nice tea gardens with excellent tea.
Large park that can get crowded on the weekends. There are several tea houses in the park. A good place to walk around, sit down, and sip a cup of tea.
Many activities and many places to drink traditional tea. Avoid the big messy tea houses and look for those hidden in quiet corners
stunning park and full of life from the nature to the people - definitely a must stop if you are in Chengdu.
Beautiful tranquil and green spot right in the middle of everything. I loved the landscaping and water feature and it was nice to see the retirees practicing ty chie and playing mahjong
Nice park to have a walk and hanging around. Beautiful lake in the middle which offer boat to hire.
The park is reachable by walking from Kuanzhai Alley. Nothing much u can do besides a park with some restaurants n coffee shops
I am quite amazed at the community activities that keep the people entertained, though I must admit there is only one drawback - the china-style toilet.
Wonderful local Teahouse experience. Beautiful evening lights. Good community activities.
great place in the city ..in the heart of the city ..Got a lot of space for public to gather and enjoy with family!!
Awesome fun to drink tea, eat sun flower seeds and people watch at one of the tea houses. Saved our rainy Sunday afternoon. :)
Interesting, green and picturious park with various activities, including singers shows, public dancing and most notable parents seeking paring for their son/duather
Really cool spot to hang out in Chengdu. Head for tea by the lake or just see the locals practice singing, tai chi and various other activities.
Always love to visit this park. Do vibrant and full of fun. Especially like the granny dancing
Great place to hang out and drink some tea with locals. There are a few beggars and peddlers, but they're not too pushy.
A nice park with Chinese features. But for me the most charming thing was Chinese woman dancing with American music.
Nice open park with food and activities. Quite a breath if fresh air in such a built up city.
Nice place. This is the place to truly experience the Chengdu people sipping tea, having some meals, and get their ears cleaned!
Hot steamy day but managed a visit for tea and a walk. Nice chance to see locals enjoying the day
Good entrance to a great park. Fair warning it was not originally created for tourists so all the information is in Chinese only.
Great park to see how chengdu people spend their spare time. Singing, dancing, speed dating, poetry...all can be seen here.
A cultural melting pot. Locals going about their leisure activities. Very friendly. Must visit
Beautiful walkways with a great tea house in the middle. Absolutely delightful on a rainy day.
Nice Central Park with local activities every days. Try the tea shop by the lake.
a little smaller than i expected, but still good for a covered tea by the lake and some good Sichuan specialty snacks
Great cup of tea from good selection of teas. Liked the dating wall Gardens lovely
The locals come together in the evenings to dance, eat and enjoy life in between the stressful moments in Chengdu.
Like almost all of parks you can visit in Chengdu this one as well looks awesome :)
Very enjoyable visit, lots of people enjoying themselves, great for people watching.
Had a wonderful time at Chengdu, China Peoples Park (South Gate) with Doctor Jing (Lily).
Full of propaganda. Interesting nontheless (and also because of it - the propaganda itself is interesting)

The People’s Park is truly beautiful, and we really enjoyed our visit. We went on a cool, slightly drizzling day, which made walking around the park even more pleasant. The lush greenery immediately impresses as you step in, creating a serene, botanical atmosphere. It’s delightful to see both locals and tourists enjoying the space. We stopped by one of the park’s tea houses, where people were leisurely drinking tea, snacking on nuts, playing games. The atmosphere is very relaxed, with visitors simply taking time to chat, unwind, and soak in the surroundings. Overall, it’s a perfect spot to take a break from sightseeing and experience Chengdu life like a local.

這裡不像那種高樓大廈林立的景點，反而多了一份老成都的市井氣息，整體的環境綠化做得很好，走在裡面感覺蠻舒服、蠻放鬆的。 最喜歡的部分還是那種隨處可見的安逸感。看著當地人聚在一起喝茶、聊天或是打牌，甚至是體驗一下路邊特有的「採耳」，這種慢步調在別的城市很難見到。如果走累了，隨便找個湖邊的茶攤坐下來，點一碗蓋碗茶，看著風景放空一陣子，整體感覺真的挺不錯。 雖然公園本身不算特別大，但機能維護得還行，動線也清楚。這裡沒什麼太商業化的壓力，就是個適合飯後散步、看看花草、觀察在地生活的地方。對我來說，這裡不需要特別安排什麼活動，單純過來感受那種「成都式的悠閒」就很值得。如果你想找個地方體驗一下當地的茶文化，這間公園算是一個很經典且保險的去處。
평일 오전에도 정말 많은 시민들이 나와서 걷고 쉬고 담소를 나눕니다. 공원 내부에 위치한 야외 음식점은 정말 큰데, 음식값이 저렴한지 많은 노인분들이 식사를 하고 계시네요. 항일전쟁 관련한 기념비나 스토리가 군데군데 보이는 그런 공원 입니다.

Парк не зря называется народный. Тут действительно много местных жителей(в основном 40+) собираются поиграть в карты, потанцевать, просто посидеть. Ну и толпы туристов, пытающихся приобщиться )). Есть пруды, и прокат лодок. Ландшафтный дизайн очень даже. Похоже на ЦПКиО или "Парк Горького", только поменьше.

Il Parco del Popolo di Chengdu è un parco completo con giardini, cultura, protezione dei cimeli culturali, educazione al patriottismo, tempo libero e intrattenimento nel suo insieme. Molto bello, molto colorato, passeggiare in questo parco è fantastico, mette il buonumore.

Một công viên tuyệt vời 👍👍👍bên trong có bán đồ ăn sáng sát bờ hồ, với combo trà đồ nướng nhẹ hoặc dimsum ... Có các bạn đi xung quanh mời làm vệ sinh tai khá thú vị ...cực đáng để trải nghiệm ...tất cả chỉ dẫn đều có tiếng anh. Mỗi nét ở đây đều mang đậm chất văn hóa truyền thống.

El Parque del Pueblo, en Chengdú, es un pulmón verde y un remanso de paz en el mismo centro de la gran ciudad (22 millones de hab.) del oeste de China. Tiene un peculiar “rincón del emparejamiento” que funciona como un tinder analógico (ver fotos): madres de chicos y chicas cuelgan carteles (rosas los de las chicas, azules los de ellos) para buscar pareja a sus hijos/as incluyendo detalles como edad, profesión, estudios o ingresos, y requisitos similares para las futuras parejas; como teléfono de contacto, el de la madre.
Công viên rộng, đông đúc, có không gian cho uống trà, ăn uống, tập thể dục, hát kịch, chèo thuyền. Có cả khu mai mối

Parco cittadino vicino alla fermata della metropolitana (People's Park) e al centro della città (piazza Tianfu). Il parco è molto grande, ricco di verde e di zone ristoro con panchine e ombra. Sono presenti anche bar e ristoranti intorno al laghetto centrale, in cui si può noleggiare delle piccole barchette per fare il giro. Sparsi nel parco si trovano molti bagni pubblici e negozi di souvenir. All'interno è facile trovare "riunioni" di pensionati cinesi che giocano a carte o ballano a ritmo di musica, un tratto tipico della cultura cinese. Alcuni turisti vengono coinvolti in maniera scherzosa nei balletti! Curiosità: All'interno si trovano le bacheche di annunci matrimoniali che gli uomini mettono, nella ricerca della moglie. Il parco è un'oasi verde nella metropoli di Chengdu, molto affollato di cinesi ma anche di turisti in cerca di refrigerio durante le calde giornate estive.

Une parenthèse vivante et paisible au cœur de Chengdu Le People’s Park est un véritable concentré de culture locale. On y croise des danseurs, des chanteurs, des joueurs de mah-jong, et même des parents qui cherchent des conjoints pour leurs enfants dans le fameux “marché aux mariages” ! Le parc est très bien entretenu, avec de jolis étangs, des allées ombragées et une ambiance chaleureuse. Ne manquez surtout pas l’expérience d’un thé traditionnel dans l’un des salons du parc – un moment authentique à vivre absolument. Une belle immersion dans la vie quotidienne des habitants de Chengdu, idéale pour faire une pause entre deux visites.

成都の人民公園（Chengdu People's Park） ​成都の人々の「スローライフ（茶館文化）」を体験できる場所として有名です。 ​場所: 成都市中心部。地下鉄の駅から直結しています。 ​歴史: 1911年に作られた、四川省で最初の公共公園です。 ​最大の特徴：茶館と耳かき ​鶴鳴茶社（Heming Teahouse）: 100年以上の歴史がある野外の茶館があり、地元の人々が竹の椅子に座って一日中お茶を飲んだり、麻雀をしたりして過ごしています。 ​耳かき: 専門の職人が、長い金属の道具を使って耳掃除をしてくれるサービスが名物です。 ​雰囲気: 上海に比べて非常にリラックスしており、地元民の日常（太極拳やダンス）に混ざってのんびり過ごすのに最適です

人民公園 - 公園載負濃厚歷史訊息；另一特色是荼園多。夏天荷花處處。公園的保路死事紀念碑，是紀念發1911年辛亥革命的前奏保路運動的死難者。碑塔的浮塑以源發的事件鐵路為題材。是歷史文物，也是公園的地標。另公園内有川軍抗日陣亡將士紀念碑及成都大轟炸紀念牆。抗日戰爭中，川軍英勇抗敵。成都這一帶被日寇猛烈轟炸。 公園的茶館歷史悠久，其中最著名的是鶴鳴荼社。現時仍時成都市民喝荼聊天玩纸牌的地方。 公園始建1911年，初名少城公園。原有中正圖書館，民眾教育館和通俗教育館建築，亦予以保留。

成都人民公园原名“少城公园”，建于1911年，占地112639平方米，是国家4A级旅游景区。悠久的历史和绝对的城市中心位置，使人民公园注定成为城市历史的见证。 在这里，可以与纪念保路运动死难烈士的“辛亥秋保路死事纪念碑”合影；可以在民国成都“六大茶馆”之首的鹤鸣茶社喝茶；也可以探寻陈寅恪、李劼人等文化名人的足迹。 另一方面，人民公园本身就是城市的活历史。那些在鹤鸣茶社吃饭、喝茶、掏耳朵的人；在人工湖上泛舟、游玩、拍照的人；甚至在“相亲角”举着牌子聊天的人，都代表着正在进行时的城市生活。
